intro: Restaurant cooks work fast, follow recipes precisely and keep a line moving. The closest of the 25 careers below is Bakers, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $37,160, about 1% less than the $37,390 restaurant cooks earn, so the pay gains come from leading a kitchen.
why_it_works: A dinner rush means timing several orders, watching temperatures and keeping stations clean. O*NET rates time management at 3 out of 5 for restaurant cooks. Baking, butchery and food production use the same skills. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The biggest pay jumps come from managing a kitchen or a restaurant, and the skills to add are maintaining and repairing equipment.
tips: Ask to run a station or train new cooks; it is the first step toward a head cook role.
Chefs and Head Cooks earn $62,470, which is 67% more, often after a certificate program.
Food Service Managers earn $69,390, or 86% more, if you like the business side.

faq.q: What jobs can former restaurant cooks do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Bakers (88%), Butchers and Meat Cutters (86%) and nonrestaurant food servers (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Food cooking machine operators are also 77% matched and earn $41,590, which is 11% more than the $37,390 restaurant cook median.

faq.q: Which careers for restaurant cooks pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more. Food Service Managers earn $69,390 (86% more), Chefs and Head Cooks $62,470 (67% more) and Carpet Installers $50,340 (35% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Head cook roles often expect a certificate or associate program.

faq.q: Do cooks need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: No. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than restaurant cooks already have. In a close match, 70% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and most training lasts one to three months on the job.

faq.q: What skills should cooks learn for a new job?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, troubleshooting, operation and control and repairing. Coordination already rates 2.62 out of 5 for restaurant cooks in O*NET, so leading a kitchen team is the main path to better pay.
